acceptance.reason: The served v31 Human surface directly reports WORKMESH_BETA_COORDINATION_MCP disabled. Existing Agent MCP verification passes, but Human Connection listing and creation cannot reach the required onboarding lifecycle, so V31-G2 through V31-G7 are not directly proven on the active deployment.

Create was rejected before a Connection fixture existed; redeem, fixture verify, revoke, durable event, and cleanup cannot be exercised. Zero successful fixture mutations occurred and no unrelated data changed.

Viewport reset and exactly-once Browser finalization pass, and runtime health/build invariance passes. The mandatory raw active request window and database fixture lifecycle readback are unavailable because the server feature gate stopped the path before an accepted fixture mutation.

finding.title: Active API and Worker omit the coordination feature binding required by the v31 Human onboarding path
evidence: The server-derived WorkMesh feature registry reports WORKMESH_BETA_COORDINATION_MCP enabled=false.
The active Human Agents page renders FEATURE_DISABLED and cannot list Connections or create the bounded fixture.
The protected API supervisor environment and retained Worker supervisor environment omit WORKMESH_BETA_COORDINATION_MCP; the v31 MCP supervisor alone sets it true.
The existing MCP Connection remains healthy, so this is an active onboarding/configuration boundary failure rather than a full runtime outage.

repair.reason: The current approval authorizes only the completed Web plus MCP replacement. Enabling the beta feature consistently requires protected API and Worker configuration/service replacement and a new bounded active-evidence attempt.
minimalScope: Version the graph with a config-only API plus Worker activation contract that binds WORKMESH_BETA_COORDINATION_MCP=true across the API, Worker, and already-active MCP roles without exposing secrets.
Independently verify exact process roots, retained protected roles, fail-closed compensation, feature registry true, and unchanged database/object-store state before one fresh Human Gate.

After approved replacement, use the remaining active Browser budget and the existing four-mutation fixture budget to rerun create, redeem, verify_connection, revoke, raw method audit, durable event, database readback, and cleanup.
